summary: Model updated for the learner-shutdown change; the update's SNAP fix holds within bounds, but the new shutdown call no longer stops or drains the follower log processor (reproduced), and a TRUNC sibling of the fixed window remains open.
validation_limits: All model checking is bounded (3 servers, MaxTxn<=2, MaxEpoch<=2, <=1 crash, <=2 learner exits); MC-full, Update-full, residual, open and discharge campaigns stopped at their time limits (LIMITED_COVERAGE).
TruncateLog, ApplySyncCommit and leaked flushes of queued writes were not observed in fresh traces (timing); they are covered by model checking only.
The prior run's stateful trace emitter was not preserved; the trace emitter was rebuilt (schema v3) and prior v2 traces were replayed on common fields only.
Data-loss consequences of MC-1/MC-2/MC-3 are model-level; only MC-1's mechanism (leaked SyncRequestProcessor) was reproduced in real code.
Adjacent duplicate WAL records are accepted by the replay-order properties (unresolved in spec/invariant-evidence.json).
The specula ci-result command is not available in this environment, so generated CI reports were not produced.

findings.title: Learner exit no longer drains or stops the follower log processor
findings.cause: Learner.shutdown now calls zk.shutdown(boolean), which LearnerZooKeeperServer does not override, so its shutdown() override that stops and drains syncProcessor is skipped.
findings.trigger: A follower leaves FOLLOWING while serving (leader stop, I/O error) or the peer shuts down; writes still queued in its SyncRequestProcessor are left to a thread that is never stopped.
findings.consequence: Thread leak on every serving learner exit (reproduced); in the model a re-synced follower's recoverable log can miss a committed txn or replay a stale record after newer ones if it crashes or reopens its log before the leaked thread writes.

premises: LearnerZooKeeperServer overrides shutdown() but not shutdown(boolean)

findings.title: TRUNC-mode learner exit before NEWLEADER keeps an unpersisted in-memory image
findings.cause: TRUNC, like SNAP, applies in-sync COMMITs only in memory until the NEWLEADER snapshot, but the update clears the database on exit only when syncMode is SNAP.
findings.trigger: A follower ahead of the leader's committed log receives TRUNC plus PROPOSAL/COMMIT for a committed-but-unapplied txn and fails before NEWLEADER, then re-joins by DIFF.
findings.consequence: The follower's recoverable log misses the committed txn; after a restart it permanently lacks it (model; pre-existing, also under exact-old semantics).

findings.title: Fast-forward before drain leaves re-sent or stale records ahead of committed history in a follower log
findings.cause: The old learner shutdown fast-forwards the DataTree before draining the sync queue, so drained txns are on disk but not in the advertised baseline and are re-sent and appended again.
findings.trigger: A serving follower exits with unflushed queued txns and re-joins by DIFF.
findings.consequence: Transiently a record follows a newer one (or an uncommitted record precedes committed ones); a crash in that window makes restart replay regress state (model; pre-existing).
